after.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
2{x}_{1}^{2}\ge -3{x}_{1}^{2},\,-{x}_{3}^{2}\ge -3{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -3{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-3(1)=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge -3.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $-3.$ But before we conclude that $-3$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=-3.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(0)^{2}-3(1)^{2}-(0)^{2} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $-3.$

after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +36) & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,7,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}=4.
$$
